case_title: Vutukuru Lakshmaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh
accused_victim_relationship: Political rival and prior enmity: the victim was a Telugu Desam supporter and a witness in a murder case in which A-1 was an accused
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302; s.148; s.324; s.149 (applied to A-5 via s.324 r/w s.149; s.149 not in charge)
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony (PW-1, PW-2, PW-3); dying declaration (Ex. P-13) recorded by a Magistrate; medical/post-mortem evidence (PW-19); recovery of weapons
aggravating_circumstances: Five stab injuries; previous animosity; victim attacked because he was a witness in a murder case
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under ss.302 and 148 IPC (and s.324 for some accused); life imprisonment under s.302 and separate sentence under s.148, concurrent
high_court_outcome: Appeal partly allowed: convictions of present appellants affirmed; A-4, A-8 and A-9 acquitted
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302, with s.148 IPC; the s.324 findings were not separately addressed
neutral_facts: At about 9.30 p.m. on the evening in question, the victim and a companion were riding a scooter near a sweet-meat shop when several persons attacked them. The rider lost control and both fell. The attackers then assaulted the victim: some stabbed him repeatedly with knives, while others beat him with iron rods. One attacker tried to stab the companion but missed, and another stabbed the companion in the left arm. The companion escaped and hid in a nearby office. Two persons returning from work saw the incident and took the injured victim to a government hospital. The companion also returned to the scene and was taken to hospital, where his statement was recorded and a case was registered. The victim was later moved to another hospital. A magistrate recorded the victim's dying declaration after confirming through the treating doctor that he was conscious; the declaration named several attackers. The victim died three days after the attack. The post-mortem examination found five stab injuries at different parts of the body and attributed death to multiple stab wounds. The investigating officer later arrested several suspects and recovered four knives and two iron rods on their instructions. The prosecution case was that the victim had been attacked because he had been a witness in an earlier murder case in which one of the attackers had been an accused.
physical_harm: Death of the victim three days after the attack from multiple stab injuries (five stab wounds); companion stabbed in left arm
number_of_offences: 3 charged (ss.302, 148, 324 IPC); 2 expressly upheld (ss.302 and 148); s.324 finding not separately addressed
premeditation_planning: Not stated; the court did not find premeditation, but noted previous animosity
motive: Accepted by the court: the victim was assaulted because he was a witness in a murder case in which A-1 was an accused
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness evidence of PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 on presence and participation; dying declaration Ex. P-13 recorded by the Magistrate (PW-18) as totally reliable; medical evidence of five stab injuries; alibi of A-1 rejected
witness_credibility: Eyewitnesses PW-2 and PW-3 found credible after keen scrutiny; the court rejected the 'chance witness' objection; dying declaration found consistent and reliable, with the Magistrate's testimony unshaken in cross-examination
trial_duration: offence: 14.05.1996; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 22.03.2007; Supreme Court: 24.04.2015
legal_representation: Appellant: Nagendra Rai, A.T.M. Rangaramanujam, P.N. Ramalingam. State: June Chaudhary, D. Mahesh Babu, Amit K. Nair, T.V. Bhaskar Reddy, Amjid Maqbool
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation completed; chargesheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Charge not framed under s.149 IPC; the court found no prejudice and did not treat it as vitiating the conviction
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted and sentenced. High Court: appeal partly allowed, convictions of appellants affirmed, A-4, A-8, A-9 acquitted. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: Dying declaration has no infirmity; eyewitnesses are credible and not chance witnesses; s.149 can be applied though not charged; not a case for conversion to s.304
defence_argument: Witnesses are chance witnesses with unreliable evidence; dying declaration is omnibus; alibi of A-1 established; s.149 cannot apply without charge; no intention to kill, so s.304 Part II should apply
legal_principle_applied: Dying declaration can ground conviction if totally reliable; absence of charge under s.149 not fatal absent prejudice; chance witness evidence requires close scrutiny; alibi requires strict proof by the accused once the prosecution establishes presence; intention judged by nature of injuries
precedent_relied_upon: Willie (William) Slaney v. State of M.P. AIR 1956 SC 116; Annareddy Sambasiva Reddy v. State of A.P. (2009) 12 SCC 546; Rana Pratap v. State of Haryana (1983) 3 SCC 327; Jarnail Singh v. State of Punjab (2009) 9 SCC 719; Mehiboobsab Abbasabi Nadaf v. State of Karnataka (2007) 13 SCC 112; Kashi Vishwanath v. State of Karnataka (2013) 7 SCC 162; Binay Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar (1997) 1 SCC 283; Gurpreet Singh v. State of Haryana (2002) 8 SCC 18; S.K. Sattar v. State of Maharashtra (2010) 8 SCC 430; Jitender Kumar v. State of Haryana (2012) 6 SCC 204; State of Orissa v. Dibakar Naik (2002) 5 SCC 323; Sunder Lal v. State of Rajasthan (2007) 10 SCC 371; Marimuthu v. State of Tamil Nadu (2008) 3 SCC 205
sentencing_rationale: Life sentence for murder upheld; conversion to s.304 Part I refused given five stab injuries and previous animosity
judicial_aggravating_factors: Five stab injuries; previous animosity; victim killed for being a witness in a murder case
